lane.name: Modern Southern rock
lane.definition: Blackberry Smoke, Whiskey Myers: Southern rock's mainstream continuation.

albums.label: Wiggy Thump Records
albums.description: Firewater is the East Texas band's breakout, mixing Skynyrd-style twin-guitar riffing with outlaw-country grit and Cody Cannon's rough-edged drawl on songs about drinking, hard times and small-town life. It established Whiskey Myers as a leading voice of the 2010s Southern-rock revival alongside Blackberry Smoke. Essential for hearing the Texas variant of the lane's sound.
albums.lineage: Extends V28's Skynyrd/Allman Southern-rock guitar lineage through a Texas outlaw-country filter, heading toward mainstream Red Dirt/Southern-rock touring circuits rather than the indie-twang Core.

albums.label: Southern Ground
albums.description: Released on Zac Brown's Southern Ground label, The Whippoorwill is Blackberry Smoke's commercial and critical breakthrough, pairing triple-guitar boogie and pedal-steel flourishes with radio-ready choruses about hard living and the open road. It represents Southern rock's mainstream 2010s revival at its most confident.
albums.lineage: Carries V28's Skynyrd/Allman/Marshall Tucker Southern-rock guitar lineage into 2010s mainstream rock and country-adjacent radio, heading toward jam-band and classic-rock revivalism rather than the punk-inflected storytelling that produced Drive-By Truckers and the Core.

albums.label: Wiggy Thump Records
albums.description: Early Morning Shakes sharpens Whiskey Myers' twin-guitar attack and adds tighter songwriting, expanding the band's audience beyond the Texas/Red Dirt circuit. It is a strong second landmark showing the band's steady climb through the 2010s Southern-rock revival. Recommended as a companion to Firewater.
albums.lineage: Continues Whiskey Myers' branch off V28's Southern-rock lineage into a wider national touring audience, still oriented toward mainstream rock radio rather than the Core.

albums.label: Rounder Records
albums.description: Blackberry Smoke's Rounder Records debut straddles rock radio and Nashville without softening its boogie-rock core, with twin guitars, organ and Charlie Starr's warm drawl. It shows Southern rock's mainstream continuation as a working, touring band rather than a nostalgia act. A solid second landmark for the band's arc.
albums.lineage: Continues Blackberry Smoke's branch off V28's Southern-rock lineage into commercial country-rock crossover, far from the Core's indie/DIY route.

albums.label: Wiggy Thump Records
albums.description: Mud pairs Whiskey Myers' Skynyrd-indebted riffing with more polished, radio-ready production and big, gang-sung choruses. It marks the point where the band's Southern-rock revival sound became fully arena-ready. A useful landmark for the lane's commercial peak.
albums.lineage: A polished entry in Whiskey Myers' branch off V28's Southern-rock lineage, aimed at mainstream rock-radio and streaming audiences rather than the DIY/indie route.

albums.label: Thirty Tigers
albums.description: The Steel Woods' debut fuses heavy, Skynyrd-and-Zeppelin-indebted riffing with outlaw-country songwriting and a cover of David Allan Coe's 'If That Ain't Country,' positioning the Nashville band between Southern rock and heavier Americana. Guitarist Jason 'Rowdy' Cope's death in 2021 cut the band's run short, making this an important document of the lane's harder-rocking wing. Essential for the heavier, storytelling-forward branch of modern Southern rock.
albums.lineage: Extends V28's Southern-rock lineage through a heavier outlaw-country filter that sounds indebted to Waylon Jennings and Skynyrd, backed by its David Allan Coe cover; closer to the Core's storytelling instincts than most of this lane but still landing in mainstream rock/Americana touring rather than indie twang.

albums.label: Tricki-Woo Records
albums.description: Sisters Rebecca and Megan Lovell push their roots-rock sound toward heavier blues-rock on Venom & Faith, built around slide guitar, stomping rhythms and reworked blues and gospel standards alongside originals. It shows a related mainstream continuation of Southern guitar-rock filtered through blues rather than boogie-rock radio. Recommended for the slide-guitar, blues-rock branch of the lane.
albums.lineage: Sounds like a blues-rock-leaning branch of V28's Southern guitar-rock lineage, indebted in particular to Allman Brothers-style slide guitar, heading toward the contemporary blues-rock circuit rather than the punk-adjacent Core.

albums.label: BMG
albums.description: Formed by the sons of three founding Allman Brothers Band members (Devon Allman, Duane Betts, Berry Duane Oakley), the Allman Betts Band's debut revives the twin-lead-guitar, jam-friendly sound of their fathers' band. It is the most literal possible continuation of Southern rock's original lineage into the present. Essential for showing the mainstream continuation as a direct family inheritance.
albums.lineage: A direct, literal continuation of V28's Allman Brothers lineage carried by the founders' own children; heads toward legacy-act jam-band touring rather than the twangier, punk-inflected Southern storytelling of the Core.

albums.label: Thirty Tigers
albums.description: Old News keeps The Steel Woods' heavy riffing intact while sharpening the band's storytelling on songs about addiction, mortality and hard-won faith. Big, twin-guitar Southern rock arrangements carry gravelly, full-throated vocals. It is a strong second album and a natural companion to the debut.
albums.lineage: Sounds indebted to V28's Southern-rock lineage, with deepening Americana songwriting; oriented toward mainstream rock/Americana audiences rather than the Core.

albums.label: Wiggy Thump Records
albums.description: The self-titled fifth album broadens Whiskey Myers' palette with horns, gospel-tinged backing vocals and slower, more reflective songs alongside the usual boogie-rock riffing. It shows a Southern-rock band mid-career trying to stretch past genre expectations without abandoning them. Recommended for hearing the band's most ambitious studio work.
albums.lineage: A more expansive, horn-and-gospel-inflected entry in Whiskey Myers' branch off V28's Southern-rock/soul lineage, still aimed at mainstream rock audiences rather than the Core.

albums.label: BMG
albums.description: Bless Your Heart stretches into longer, more improvisational arrangements than the debut, closer to the Allman Brothers' live-jam tradition. It doubles down on the band's role as caretakers of their fathers' sound rather than pushing toward reinvention. Recommended as a second, jammier landmark.
albums.lineage: Continues the Allman Betts Band's direct-inheritance branch off V28, leaning further into the jam-band side of Southern rock rather than toward the Core's more compact songwriting.

albums.label: 3 Legged / Thirty Tigers
albums.description: Co-produced by Dave Cobb, You Hear Georgia leans into big, radio-friendly hooks while keeping the band's triple-guitar Southern-rock foundation intact, with guest turns from Warren Haynes and Jamey Johnson. It shows the band still drawing A-list Southern-music collaborators well into its third decade.
albums.lineage: A recent entry in Blackberry Smoke's ongoing branch off V28's Southern-rock lineage, produced by Dave Cobb, whose work elsewhere ties the mainstream and Americana wings of Southern music together without pulling this record into the Core.

albums.label: Tricki-Woo Records
albums.description: Blood Harmony pairs the Lovell sisters' close harmonies and slide-guitar riffing with some of the band's most polished, big-room production. The songs lean on stomping blues-rock grooves and hooky choruses rather than long jams. A strong recent landmark for the blues-rock wing of Southern rock's mainstream continuation.
albums.lineage: Continues Larkin Poe's slide-guitar blues-rock, which sounds indebted to V28's Southern guitar lineage; distinct from both the boogie-rock (Blackberry Smoke) and jam-band (Allman Betts) wings of the same lane.
